topicName: Azure Load Balancer, Application Gateway, and Front Door
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Comprehensive Guide to Azure Load Balancing Services"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Designing a scalable and highly available architecture in Microsoft Azure requires choosing the right load-balancing solution. Azure provides several options tailored for different layers of the OSI model and routing requirements. This tutorial covers Azure Load Balancer, Azure Application Gateway, and Azure Front Door."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Azure Load Balancer"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 (Transport layer) of the OSI model. It delivers high performance and ultra-low latency for TCP and UDP protocols. It is ideal for high-availability scenarios for both inbound and outbound flows."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer: Layer 4 (TCP/UDP)"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope: Regional (Public or Internal/Private)"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Cases: High-performance TCP/UDP apps, gaming, and non-HTTP protocols."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Azure Application Gateway"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Application Gateway is a web traffic (OSI Layer 7) load balancer that enables you to manage traffic to your web applications. It supports features like SSL termination, cookie-based session affinity, and URL path-based routing."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer: Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS/WebSocket)"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope: Regional"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Cases: Web applications requiring URL routing, SSL offloading, and Web Application Firewall (WAF) protection."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Azure Front Door"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Front Door is a modern cloud content delivery network (CDN) and global Layer 7 load balancer. It provides fast, reliable, and secure access between users and your global web content with instant failover."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer: Layer 7 (Global HTTP/HTTPS)"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope: Global (Anycast)"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Cases: Global web applications, content acceleration, and instant multi-region failover."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Deploying an Azure Load Balancer using Azure CLI"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example of how to create a basic public standard Azure Load Balancer using the Azure CLI."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"az network lb create --resource-group \"myResourceGroup\" --name \"myLoadBalancer\" --sku \"Standard\" --public-ip-address \"myPublicIP\" --frontend-ip-name \"myFrontEnd\" --backend-pool-name \"myBackEndPool\""},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Selecting the correct load balancer depends entirely on your traffic profile. Use Azure Load Balancer for Layer 4 regional transport, Application Gateway for regional Layer 7 web routing, and Front Door for global Layer 7 application delivery."}]
